memory_leads.lead: Navigation execution spans distinct roles: shore/company operations can set commercial or routing constraints; the master retains onboard command; officer of the watch and bridge team execute and monitor; pilots and vessel-traffic or port-control functions add local interfaces; hydrographic/chart and weather-routeing functions supply information without becoming the vessel's command chain.

Voyage appraisal, passage-plan preparation, onboard review or approval, briefing and actual execution are separate states. A plan can exist before departure yet later require amendment; an executed track must not be backfilled as if it were the originally intended plan.

Chart or ENC readiness is its own information state: required coverage, edition or update/correction status, display/configuration readiness and known limitations can change on different clocks from the physical operability of bridge equipment. Exact chart identifiers and correction histories require Evidence.

Weather and routeing inputs are dynamic decision inputs rather than final route facts. Forecasts, observed conditions, traffic or security constraints, draft/under-keel or port timing considerations and commercial ETA/fuel objectives can trigger route or speed reconsideration without proving that any particular route was optimal.

Bridge-watch readiness is more than crew certification: watch composition, handover, standing instructions, fatigue/workload, visibility/traffic context and equipment status determine the contemporaneous bridge-team state. Exact watch schedules and legal requirements remain source-specific.

Pilotage is a handoff layer rather than command transfer in the abstract: pilot ordering/boarding readiness, master-pilot information exchange, local passage understanding, bridge-team integration and pilot disembarkation can occur on different clocks. Exact responsibilities and rules are jurisdiction-specific.

Position monitoring should be represented as repeated observations and cross-checks rather than one authoritative coordinate. Independent sensor or visual/radar-type fixes, charted position, track error, depth or other contextual checks can disagree or degrade; a later casualty finding must not be retroactively treated as the bridge team's contemporaneous knowledge.

Traffic and collision-avoidance management is a sequence of detected target/context state, assessment, bridge-team communication, maneuver or speed decision, execution and re-assessment. The structural chain can be remembered while exact actions, rules, fault and safe maneuver conclusions remain Evidence/legal territory.

Navigation-equipment availability is multidimensional: equipment can be fully available, degraded, alarmed, under workaround, isolated for defect or awaiting service while the vessel's overall operating status remains a separate decision. This connects navigation readiness to P057's defect backlog without inventing a vessel deficiency.

Deviation and replanning form a durable transition: new information or operating constraints can prompt proposed deviation, master/bridge reassessment, shore notification or commercial coordination where relevant, amended plan, execution and record. Original and revised intentions should both survive for point-in-time replay.

Port approach and departure navigation create a coordination boundary among bridge team, pilot, VTS/port control and ship-side port-call execution. Arrival time, pilot/traffic windows and navigational readiness can constrain each other even when berth, cargo and agency services are otherwise ready.

Navigation records have separate event-time and known-time value: bridge logs, position or course records, plan amendments, pilot-exchange records and automated recordings can preserve different slices of the contemporaneous picture. The existence of a record does not by itself prove its completeness, correctness or causal meaning.

Bridge resource management is an operating-state concept: information sharing, challenge/escalation, workload distribution, situational awareness and handover quality can affect execution, but blind Memory must not rank crew quality or infer human error from later outcomes.

P060 safety-management memory is refined because controlled procedures, risk assessments and drills become real only through bridge execution, monitoring and replanning; documentary SMS readiness and actual navigational readiness are related but not identical states.

P059 crewing memory is refined because holding valid qualifications and being onboard do not automatically establish bridge-watch readiness: handover, fatigue/workload, role assignment, pilot integration and information state still matter.

P057 technical-management memory is refined because a navigation-equipment defect can create degraded operating arrangements, extra cross-check burden, service demand or operational restrictions without automatically proving off-hire or unseaworthiness.

The atlas effective-capacity and fuel/speed themes are refined because weather, routeing, traffic constraints and deviation decisions can alter voyage distance, speed profile, ETA and fuel use without changing nominal fleet capacity.
P054 already covers casualty occurrence, emergency response and investigation. P061 stops before post-casualty causation and adds the pre-event navigation execution/monitoring state instead.

P052 already covers pilot/tug/port-call service coordination from the ship-agent side. P061 reuses that boundary only for bridge/pilot/VTS navigation execution rather than duplicating port-agency workflow.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Exact navigational content and information vintages require vessel- and voyage-specific authoritative Evidence.
Specific actions and fault/safety conclusions are high-stakes operational/legal matters requiring Evidence and context.
These are vessel-, company- and jurisdiction-specific source facts.
Provider identity, current capability and ranking claims require source-first research outside blind Memory.

stop_reason: The navigation/bridge layer is populated from appraisal and passage planning through information readiness, bridge watch/handover, pilot/VTS interfaces, position cross-check, traffic decision, equipment state, deviation/replanning and records. Further recall becomes route-, waypoint-, chart-, watch-log-, maneuver-, pilotage-, provider- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation and not navigation, safety, regulatory, pilotage, collision-avoidance, operational or legal advice; no route, waypoint, chart/ENC status, weather recommendation, watch arrangement, pilotage requirement, position, maneuver, fault, record completeness, provider capability or jurisdictional conclusion is verified.
